summary:
This bill, the “Halting the Epidemic of Addiction and Loss Act of 2025,” directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to ensure that references to opioid overdose reversal agents in certain departmental grant programs are not limited to naloxone but are inclusive of other FDA-approved or authorized drugs.

Section 2(a) imposes a prospective requirement: whenever the Department of Health and Human Services issues a regulation or guidance for any grant program addressing opioid misuse and use disorders, the Secretary shall ensure, as appropriate, that any reference to an opioid overdose reversal drug (such as naloxone) is inclusive of any opioid overdose reversal drug approved under section 505 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 355) for emergency treatment of a known or suspected opioid overdose.

Section 2(b) addresses existing references. Not later than one year after enactment, the Secretary must update all references to an opioid overdose reversal drug (such as naloxone) in any HHS regulation or guidance issued before enactment that is part of two specified grant programs: (1) the State and Tribal response to opioid use disorders grant program under section 1003 of the 21st Century Cures Act (42 U.S.C. 290ee-3a), commonly known as State Opioid Response Grants and Tribal Opioid Response Grants; and (2) the grant program for priority substance use disorder prevention needs of regional and national significance under section 516 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 290bb-22). For these existing references, the update must make them inclusive of any opioid overdose reversal drug that has been approved or otherwise authorized for use by the Food and Drug Administration—a broader category than the prospective requirement’s reference to section 505 approval alone.

The bill contains no appropriations, authorizations of appropriations, or sunset provisions. It establishes a mandatory duty for the Secretary, qualified by the phrase “as appropriate” in the prospective provision, and sets a one-year deadline for the retrospective update.
